final_answer:
Depth-first search (DFS) and breadth-first search (BFS) are algorithms used to traverse or search graphs. DFS explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, using a stack (or recursion) to keep track of nodes. BFS, on the other hand, explores all neighbors at the current depth level before moving to the next level, using a queue.  

DFS is memory efficient for deep trees but risks getting stuck in cycles if not managed, while BFS guarantees finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs but uses more memory.  

Choose DFS when memory is limited, for problems requiring path exploration (e.g., mazes), or when the target is likely deep in the graph. Choose BFS for finding the shortest path, in unweighted graphs, or when the solution is closer to the root. Safe.
